# ENEL445 Exam Prep Hub

This folder is the central exam-prep entry point across the three prepared study packs:

- Roy Smith optimisation block: `../Roy_Smith_ETH`
- Game theory: `../GameTheory`
- Power systems optimisation: `../Week_7_Power_Systems_Optimisation`

It also connects to the actual exam/test evidence:

- Past exams: `../PastExams`
- Past tests: `../PastTests`

Do not copy all raw files into this folder. Use this hub as the map, then jump to the right source file.

## Confirmed 2026 Exam Reality

Based on the exam information you provided:

- Exam duration: 2 hours.
- Cheat sheet: one A4 double-sided page, same as for the test.
- Calculator allowed.
- Format: two questions worth 20 marks each, 40 marks total.
- Q1: set by Prof. Roy Smith, on Roy's material.
- Q2: set by the Term 2 lecturer, mixed Term 2 material, with some Term 1 knowledge required.
- Q2 includes power systems, game theory, and linear matrix inequalities.
- The exam is more mathematical than last year's exam: expect more calculations and fewer pure explanation questions.

Past exams are still useful for style and templates, but their old four-question structure is not the 2026 structure.

## Training Consequence

Train as two 20-mark papers:

| Exam question | Main source | Training mode |
|---|---|---|
| Q1 Roy Smith | `../Roy_Smith_ETH` | least squares, regularisation, convexity, cones, LMI/Schur complement, MPC/KKT |
| Q2 Term 2 mixed | `../Week_7_Power_Systems_Optimisation`, `../GameTheory`, Roy LMI sections, Term 1 basics | power-system LS/OPF, payoff matrix/game theory, LMI conversions, KKT/math basics |

Because the exam is more mathematical, do not spend most time memorising prose. Spend most time doing:

- write the optimisation problem;
- define variables and matrices;
- derive gradients, KKT conditions, and closed forms;
- transform constraints into standard or LMI form;
- convert quadratic/SOC constraints using Schur complement;
- solve small payoff-matrix/game questions;
- formulate DC/AC power-system least-squares problems.

## Past Exam Use

Older past exams show useful question styles, but their coverage should be downweighted where it is not in the confirmed 2026 scope.

Use old papers mainly for:

1. mathematical derivations;
2. least-squares formulations;
3. KKT and constrained optimisation basics;
4. power systems Q4-style questions;
5. one-line game theory questions.

Downweight old algorithm-heavy sections such as Nelder-Mead, DIRECT, GA, PSO, Hungarian, transportation, and branch-and-bound unless your lecturer explicitly said they remain examinable.

## Two-Day Priority

If time is short, do not read everything linearly. Train by question type:

1. Formulation questions:
   - least squares;
   - nonlinear least squares;
   - MPC;
   - power-system state estimation;
   - LP standard form.

2. Derivation questions:
   - gradient of quadratic form;
   - Taylor expansion;
   - Newton step;
   - ridge regression closed form;
   - KKT conditions.

3. Short explanation questions:
   - AC OPF vs DC OPF;
   - SC-OPF;
   - Nash equilibrium;
   - dominant strategy;
   - why LMI constraints are convex;
   - why Schur complement is useful.

4. Small calculation questions:
   - exact line search for a quadratic;
   - simple LP/QP standard form;
   - power-system LS matrix setup;
   - payoff matrix best responses;
   - Schur complement / LMI conversion.

## Files in This Hub

- `two_day_training_plan.qmd`: concrete 2-day schedule.

## Future Prompt Pattern

Use this when asking Codex for training:

```text
Use exam_prep/README.qmd as the hub. Train me on [topic] from basic level to exam level.
First teach the concept, then give 3 progressive questions, then mark my answer.
```

For a timed drill:

```text
Use exam_prep/exam_question_map.qmd. Give me a 20-minute mini exam on [topic].
After I answer, grade strictly and show the shortest exam-ready solution.
```
